knowledge_point.title: Solving for a Vector in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of ${x}_{1}-{x}_{4}$ given that  $6a-2x=b$ and

$$
a=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,x=\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}10 \\ -4 \\ -12 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6a-2x & =b \\ -2x & =b-6a \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}(b-6a) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}(\begin{bmatrix}10 \\ -4 \\ -12 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}-6\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ 2 \\ 12 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ x & =\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -1 \\ -6 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}-{x}_{4}=7-1=6.$

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}$ given that $3a-5x=b$ and

$$
a=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,x=\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-23 \\ 5 \\ 42\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3a-5x & =b \\ -5x & =b-3a \\ x & =-\frac{1}{5}(b-3a) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{5}(\begin{bmatrix}-23 \\ 5 \\ 42\end{bmatrix}-3\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}-35 \\ 5 \\ 30\end{bmatrix} \\ x & =\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -1 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=7-1=6.$
